subsystems.name: Bioprinter hardware
subsystems.role: deposits living cells and structural gels in a precise 3D pattern.
parts: optical or DLP light source for light-cured gels

subsystems.name: Bioinks
subsystems.role: carry the cells and set into a soft, cell-friendly matrix.

subsystems.name: Vascular design software
subsystems.role: generates a branching channel tree that can actually be printed and perfused.
parts: imaging data from CT or MRI scans

subsystems.name: Endothelial lining
subsystems.role: coats each channel so it behaves like a real blood vessel wall.

subsystems.name: Perfusion and maturation
subsystems.role: pumps oxygen and nutrients through the channels and lets the tissue mature.

subsystems.name: Quality control
subsystems.role: checks that channels are open, leak-free and correctly lined.

buildSteps.title: Map the vasculature
buildSteps.detail: Scan the target tissue, then use image data to design a branching channel tree down to vessels a few hundred micrometres across.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the inks
buildSteps.detail: Mix a cell-laden hydrogel for the tissue bulk and a sacrificial ink that can be printed and later washed out.

buildSteps.title: Co-axial print
buildSteps.detail: In one pass, a nozzle extrudes the sacrificial ink as a core surrounded by the cell-laden gel, laying down hollow precursors inside the tissue.

buildSteps.title: Crosslink and stack
buildSteps.detail: The hydrogel is gelled by light, temperature or ions, and the process repeats layer by layer into a thick construct.

buildSteps.title: Evacuate the channels
buildSteps.detail: The sacrificial core is dissolved or melted out, leaving an open, interconnected lumen.

buildSteps.title: Seed the lining
buildSteps.detail: Endothelial cells are perfused through the channels and allowed to attach, forming a barrier like a blood-vessel wall.

buildSteps.title: Perfuse and mature
buildSteps.detail: Culture medium is pumped through the network in a bioreactor for days to weeks so the tissue survives and differentiates.

buildSteps.title: Test or implant
buildSteps.detail: Constructs are used for drug testing, or, in animal trials, connected to a host blood supply.

prerequisites.why: the core technique for carving channels, demonstrated with simple tissues but not at organ scale.

prerequisites.tech: Soft hydrogels with the right stiffness and printability
prerequisites.why: gels soft enough for cells are often too weak to hold millimetre-scale channels open.

prerequisites.tech: Vascular cell biology and endothelial culture
prerequisites.why: the lining must stay alive, non-clotting and leak-tight under flow.
without flow, tissue thicker than roughly a millimetre starves of oxygen.

prerequisites.tech: Printing true capillaries below about 10 µm
prerequisites.why: no printing method yet matches the finest vessels that reach every cell in a real organ.

pathway.milestone: millimetre-scale perfusable tissue chips for drug testing
pathway.unlocks: more realistic toxicity and disease models, cutting some animal testing.

pathway.milestone: vascularised implantable patches and organ-on-chip systems
pathway.unlocks: repair of thin or simple tissues and better predictors of human drug response.

pathway.milestone: centimetre-thick vascularised constructs that survive after grafting
pathway.unlocks: repair of larger injuries and eventually simple organ subunits.

pathway.milestone: whole printed organs with a full hierarchical vessel tree
pathway.unlocks: an alternative to donor waiting lists, if capillary-scale vessels and long-term safety can be achieved.
